sources.title: Quadratic Hecke Sums and Mass Equidistribution
selectors: Proposition 3.1, lines 444-484 in current publisher HTML
sources.classified_claim: Proposition 3.1 applies Friedberg–Hoffstein Theorem B to produce infinitely many quadratic characters with a nonzero central twist while imposing finite local quadratic-character behavior; the proof reduces to sign compatibility. The paper explicitly says negative D could be used. Equation (4.2) gives L(pi_D,s)=L(pi,s)L(pi tensor chi_D,s).
sources.limitations: The article's quaternionic/automorphic setup is not identical to the Fornea–Gehrmann plectic setup; it does not itself verify every plectic local/residual hypothesis for arbitrary E.

sources.title: Nonvanishing theorems for automorphic L-functions on GL(2)
selectors: Theorem B as invoked explicitly in Nelson Proposition 3.1
sources.classified_claim: Primary original nonvanishing source behind the finite-local-prescription application. Exact theorem text was not available in the current official-page parser, so the scoped theorem-use is bound through the later primary paper's explicit application rather than reconstructed from memory.
sources.limitations: Do not infer unparsed hypotheses beyond what the source-bound application establishes.

sources.title: Iwasawa theory and mock plectic points
sources.classified_claim: The plectic setup takes an imaginary quadratic K with p inert, N unramified, N^- the inert part of N/p square-free with even number of prime factors, and residual hypotheses. Nonvanishing Q_K together with L(E/K,1)=0 is an input to the p-Selmer conclusion; Q_K nonvanishing is not deduced from complex analytic rank. Example 1.5 exhibits a rank-two-over-Q triple with mixed inert/split local pattern, but is only an example.
sources.limitations: Does not prove complex second derivative => Q_K != 0; does not prove full Mordell–Weil/Sha/leading-term BSD.

sources.title: Plectic Heegner classes
selectors: construction/comparison sections as audited in R3
sources.classified_claim: Constructs partially global plectic Heegner classes recovering plectic Heegner points and mock plectic invariants through localization/projection. Higher-rank arithmetic significance remains outside the theorem needed here.
sources.limitations: No theorem in the bounded audit derives root-faithful plectic nonvanishing from the complex s-second derivative.

sources.title: Plectic points and Hida-Rankin p-adic L-functions
sources.classified_claim: Provides a p-adic Gross–Zagier formula computing higher derivatives of Hida–Rankin p-adic L-functions in terms of plectic points.
sources.limitations: The derivative coordinate is p-adic/Hida–Rankin, not the complex s derivative of L(E/K,s). The regulator interpretation in higher rank is conjectural in the source framing.

sources.authors: Víctor Hernández Barrios; Santiago Molina Blanco
sources.title: Exceptional zero formulas for anticyclotomic p-adic L-functions
sources.classified_claim: Relates r-th derivatives of anticyclotomic p-adic L-functions to plectic points and Tate periods in an exceptional-zero setting.
sources.limitations: Again a p-adic derivative coordinate, not the complex s-second derivative.

assumptions: E/Q is an elliptic curve with ord_{s=1} L(E,s)=2
K/Q is quadratic with character chi_K and E^K is the quadratic twist
quadratic base change factorization L(E/K,s)=L(E,s)L(E^K,s) at the compatible L-function normalization
exact_local_derivation.proof_note: Because exact order two gives L(E,1)=L'(E,1)=0 and L''(E,1)!=0, differentiating the source-bound product twice leaves only L''(E,1)L(E^K,1) at s=1.
exact_local_derivation.scope: stored-factorization + elementary Taylor composition; no new deep theorem

positive_evidence: Friedberg–Hoffstein as explicitly applied by Nelson allows finite local quadratic-character prescriptions subject to a compatible global root sign.
Nelson notes negative discriminants are equally possible in that application.
Fornea–Gehrmann requires an even number of inert N^- primes, giving epsilon(E/K)=+1 rather than an immediate parity contradiction.
unclosed_binding: The exact Fornea–Gehrmann pattern p inert / conductor primes split or inert as required must be instantiated simultaneously with central twist nonvanishing for the target E.
Residual surjectivity and ramification hypotheses in Fornea–Gehrmann depend on E,p,N^- and are not supplied merely by selecting K.

The bounded audit did not source-bind a single theorem stated exactly as 'for every analytic-rank-two E/Q satisfying a plectic-eligible prime condition, choose an admissible imaginary K with L(E^K,1)!=0'.
